races.name: bet365 Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Rated highest in the field at OR 140 but his form string (804-54) is modest and his similar-going record reads 0 wins from 1 placement; racing prominently suits this field map and Cobden/Mullins add obvious class, but the STYLE_FIT flag means he may not dominate as convincingly as his rating implies.

runners_data.name: Pony Soprano
runners_data.note: Two recent wins and places on Good ground (sim-going: 1W3P from 3 runs) make him the most in-form hold-up runner here; Harry Skelton is an astute judge of pace in small fields, and the tongue-strap (tp) suggests he's been produced optimally, though his weight and hold-up reliance leave him vulnerable if the tempo never quickens.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Won just 12 days ago over a similar distance on Good, giving her a freshness edge over rivals who are 34 days off the track; Mickey Bowen's yard is quietly consistent (4/20 over 14 days) and her record of 1W4P in similar going highlights durable consistency, making her a worthy threat if she runs prominently as the small field allows.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the sole confirmed front-runner in this three-runner contest and will set a controlled, uncontested pace over the 2m4f trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. With no rival likely to challenge for the lead, Sony Bill can dictate his own rhythm, avoiding the energy cost of a pace battle and potentially keeping something in reserve for the final fences. Pony Soprano and Tamarind Bay are both hold-up types who will track from behind, meaning the race will likely be run at a steady-to-fair gallop with a tactical finish developing from the home turn. This race shape — a lone front-runner controlling tempo — strongly favours closers with a sharp turn of foot over this trip on Good ground, and both hold-up runners are better placed to exploit any late acceleration than Sony Bill is to repel them if the pace is honest enough to set them alight.

scenarios.body: If Pony Soprano times his challenge to perfection, with Harry Skelton delivering him late to score decisively over rivals who have peaked too soon.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sony Bill's jumping — if he makes any errors at the fences while setting the pace alone, Pony Soprano and Tamarind Bay will be perfectly positioned to capitalise immediately given the tiny field.

Tamarind Bay's short turnaround (12 days since last run) is a positive fitness angle but monitor her in the paddock; if she shows any fatigue signs it could undermine her chance against fresher rivals at the finish.

With only three runners, any incident or unseated rider — particularly at the first fence where horses are still finding their stride — could dramatically alter the race shape and produce an unusual result.

Pony Soprano's headgear (tongue-strap) is worth noting as a yard-confidence signal from Dan Skelton; if he travels sweetly behind Sony Bill without pulling, he will arrive at the final fences with every chance of winning a sustained duel.

The Good ground across all races today at Uttoxeter appears consistent and true — no significant rail or ground bias reported — meaning pace-shape rather than ground positioning will be the decisive tactical factor in this contest.

races.name: Never Ordinary At bet365 Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Flying Ace
runners_data.note: Won two of his last three over 20f on Good ground and boasts strong recent form (3-4-4-1-1); Harry Skelton will roll forward from the front, controlling tempo entirely on his own terms with no other confirmed leader in the field.

runners_data.name: Jetbob
runners_data.note: Sole hurdles run produced a win over 20f on Good ground, which aligns well with today's conditions; prominent style means Ben Poste can slot in just off Flying Ace, though a 58-day absence and a thin profile (just one hurdle run) introduces uncertainty about his current sharpness.

runners_data.name: Not Now
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old with just two hurdle runs and a long 215-day absence since last seen; hood worn previously and hold-up style means Sam Twiston-Davies needs the pace to be genuine to land a blow, which looks unlikely in this controlled scenario.

runners_data.name: Way Maker
runners_data.note: Recent form of 1-1-0-3-2 shows consistent competitiveness, including a second over 20f on Good ground; James Bowen can position him prominently behind Flying Ace, and his course-relevant experience over the right trip and going makes him the most obvious beneficiary if the leader weakens.

runners_data.name: Moi Mon Vieux
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who has placed twice on Good ground over shorter trips; tongue-tie fitted and Jonathan Burke will need a strong gallop to get him into it from the back, but his trip profile (best form at 16f) raises questions about whether 2m4f on a turning track will fully suit.

races.paceDynamic: Flying Ace is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, Harry Skelton can dictate terms at whatever tempo he chooses over the 2m4f trip on Good ground. Way Maker and Jetbob both carry prominent-running profiles and will likely sit just off the leader's heels, but neither is an aggressive front-runner who will force Flying Ace into a contested gallop. Not Now and Moi Mon Vieux are hold-up horses who will be ridden from the back, meaning the pace is entirely in Flying Ace's control and is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than searching. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and those tracking close to a controlled pace, as hold-up horses will need a meaningful injection of tempo late in the race to close the gap — and with no one applying early pressure, that injection is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.title: Flying Ace Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Flying Ace dictates an uncontested, sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses are never given the pace injection they need.
scenarios.body: If Flying Ace dictates an uncontested, sustainable gallop and the hold-up horses are never given the pace injection they need.

scenarios.title: Prominents Pounce Late

scenarios.body: If Flying Ace sets a genuine gallop and ties himself up late, leaving Way Maker or Jetbob to sweep past approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly

scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and Moi Mon Vieux or Not Now close powerfully from the back.

scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Pounces

watchPoints.text: Flying Ace's jumping must be monitored — any significant error mid-race immediately brings Way Maker and Jetbob into sharp contention given how close they will be tracking him.
Not Now's 215-day absence is a notable flag; if he returns noticeably ring-rusty or short of fitness, he may drop out tamely from the back and distort any late sectional reads.
Way Maker's ability to find a position close to Flying Ace early is key — if he gets boxed out or slots further back than ideal in a small five-runner field, his chance is materially reduced.

Jetbob's single hurdles run means his jumping under race pressure is an unknown quantity; watch his technique at the early flights to assess whether Ben Poste can maintain his prominent position safely.

Moi Mon Vieux is fitted with a tongue-tie today — first-time headgear runners can produce unexpected performances, and Jonathan Burke may choose to ride him with more aggression than his usual hold-up tag suggests.

races.name: bet365 Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gunsight Ridge
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will set the pace uncontested; trainer Sowersby is 0/4 in 14 days, sim-going record is a modest 1 place from 2 runs, and at 11 years old over 2m on Good the likelihood of him sustaining to the line rather than just controlling matters is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a strong prominent-running profile and three wins from six places on similar going; the 225-day absence is the main flag, but Anthony Honeyball's horses often return fit and Sam Twiston-Davies is a sharp pilot at tracks like Uttoxeter over 2m.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Has won three of his last four starts including back-to-back on Good and Soft, Oakley Brown's 5lb claim is a live asset, and the tongue-tie is retained; 21 days since last run feels fresh rather than stale and the prominent style is perfectly aligned with this race's expected shape.

runners_data.name: Coastguard Station
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with an outstanding 14-from-15 record on similar Going and two wins in 2024-25; at OR=123 and age 10 he is reliable rather than progressive, but his consistency on Good ground means he is never far away if the pace creates late openings.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: At 12 years old he retains a tidy profile of Good-ground placed efforts and ran well latest at OR=123; the hold-up style means he needs something to go wrong up front to get involved, but his jumping solidity makes him a salvage option if attrition bites.

runners_data.name: Kingston Narcissus
runners_data.note: Trainer Dan Skelton is in fine form (17/31 in 14 days) and Harry Skelton is a top jockey, and the horse won at this OR on Good ground recently — however his natural prominent style means he'll have to push past rivals early to claim a berth, adding risk and energy cost that tempers expectations in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Gris Majeur
runners_data.note: Won most recently on Good at OR=117 and boasts an excellent placed record (2W/7P on similar going); a true hold-up performer whose position in the midfield bracket on the map is a consequence of the field's make-up rather than a change of tactics — needs a proper gallop to deliver his finish and this pace scenario is unlikely to suit fully.

races.paceDynamic: Gunsight Ridge is the confirmed pace-setter here and, with no genuine challenger pressing for the lead, he should control proceedings at a comfortable, sustainable gallop over this sharp 2m Uttoxeter circuit. Breaking Cover and Newtown Rambler will look to sit prominently just off his heels, meaning the early order is likely to be orderly and unhurried rather than frenetically contested. That controlled tempo on Good ground over a flat-ish 2m track tends to compress the field and keep it together until the last two fences, when a short burst of acceleration decides the verdict — a scenario that suits prominent, travelling horses who can quicken rather than deep closers who need a truly searching gallop to grind rivals down. The field holds more prominent-running types than the map can accommodate: Kingston Narcissus is a natural P-style horse who will likely be shuffled back against his will, while Gris Majeur is a genuine hold-up performer who ends up mapped in midfield by default — in practice Newtown Rambler and Breaking Cover are best-placed to secure the prominent berths behind Gunsight Ridge.

scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins

scenarios.body: If Gunsight Ridge sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race is only properly ignited from the second-last fence.

scenarios.body: If Gunsight Ridge sets a faster-than-expected clip and ties up before the last, opening the door for the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Kingston Narcissus Overcomes Redistribution
scenarios.trigger: If Kingston Narcissus manages to push forward from his allotted midfield position and secures a prominent berth despite the crowded early orders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Grinding Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively taxing on the Good ground and the contest becomes a slog of jumping accuracy and stamina from the fourth-last.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves deceptively taxing on the Good ground and the contest becomes a slog of jumping accuracy and stamina from the fourth-last.

watchPoints.text: Newtown Rambler's jockey Oakley Brown (5lb claimer) must secure a clean prominent position early; if he gets squeezed out behind Breaking Cover and Gunsight Ridge at the first fence, the horse's entire tactical advantage evaporates.

Breaking Cover returns after 225 days off — watch the market move and the paddock demeanour closely; a flat jumper or one blowing hard after the first circuit would signal the layoff has blunted his sharpness.

Kingston Narcissus will be fighting for a berth that may not be available; if Harry Skelton can't slot in behind the leaders before the third fence, the horse will be racing well out of his comfort zone for the rest of the 2m trip.

Gunsight Ridge's jumping accuracy at the last few fences is the hinge point of the race — if he pings the third-last and second-last cleanly, he stays competitive; if he makes an error under pressure he is likely to be passed by at least two rivals in the final 100 yards.

Gris Majeur is worth monitoring from the back — if the pace is genuinely steady and the field bunches turning in, his finishing effort could close the gap faster than his odds suggest, particularly if Coastguard Station or Sir Tivo don't travel as smoothly as expected.

races.name: bet365 Summer Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hang In There
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter and race-shaper; Emma Lavelle's 12-year-old is in good form (won last time out) and has course-going credentials, but age and the weight of 168lbs over 3m on Good ground is a stamina concern in the final furlong; the race is genuinely his to lose from the front.

runners_data.name: Riskintheground
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's hold-up operator arrives on the back of a win 21 days ago and is 3W4P on Good ground, making the going combination ideal; Harry Skelton knows how to position a hold-up horse in a slowly-run race, and the 3m trip on this surface looks well within range.

runners_data.name: Twig
runners_data.note: Prominent-running veteran who has won twice on Good ground and ticks the going box; Beau Morgan's claim is useful at these weights, and the 3m trip is squarely in his range — a clean round of jumping from just off Hang In There is the scenario that suits him most.

runners_data.name: Alien Storm
runners_data.note: David Bass partners this Charlie Longsdon-trained eight-year-old who is in excellent form (four of last five finishes in the frame) and handles Good ground well; a prominent runner who should slot in naturally behind the leader without fighting for position in this field.

runners_data.name: Ki Woo
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent type who won last time out and has 3W4P on similar going; the Greenall/Guerriero yard is in fair form (5/21 in 14 days) and at six years old Ki Woo is the youngest in the field, which suggests untapped stamina for this 3m test.

runners_data.name: Peaky Boy
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes the ride on this consistent if unspectacular prominent runner; Good-ground form is fine but recent finishing positions of 3-3 suggest a horse finding its level rather than one about to bolt up, and the step to 3m is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Hold Your Fort
runners_data.note: Callum Pritchard partners this hold-up specialist who is 3W7P on Good ground — a standout stat — and the 3m trip suits given two of those wins came at 24f-26f; the Debra Hamer yard shows 0/0 in the last 14 days but the horse arrives 55 days fresh.

runners_data.name: Queensbury Boy
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's seven-year-old has won at 25f on Good ground and finished second last time; a prominent runner who should track the pace naturally but faces a slight step up in trip to 3m — stamina resolution will decide whether he can sustain his effort.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: Prolific winner on Good ground (7W10P) and a natural front-runner by instinct; with Hang In There ahead, Bryan Carver will struggle to get the position this horse needs, and racing out of a held-up role blunts its chance meaningfully in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Grand Clermont
runners_data.note: David Pipe's ten-year-old won at 24f on Good ground recently and is a natural pace-seeker; Lucas Murphy (7) takes the ride, but with multiple prominent types ahead of him in the queue, he is likely to be shuffled wider than ideal and his Good-ground figures (3/15) are modest by comparison.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's hold-up horse won last time out at 23f on Good ground and arrives 17 days fresh; 3W5P on similar going is solid and the 3m trip is slightly beyond his proven best, but a strongly run finish would bring him into contention late.

runners_data.name: Regarde
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner by preference who consistently finishes placed on Good ground (4W9P); Jamie Snowden's nine-year-old will find himself racing further back than he'd like given the congestion ahead, and Gavin Sheehan will need to be creative to compensate.

runners_data.name: Imperial Alex
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's nine-year-old is in decent form (1-2 last two starts on Good ground) and Stan Sheppard rides; a prominent runner at heart who is displaced into midfield by the field's pace composition, which limits the probability that his natural racing style can be expressed.

runners_data.name: Stratagem
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner; Mickey Bowen's ten-year-old has a good record on Good ground (3W5P) and over 26f+ trips, so if declared would be a natural mapfield type — but the non-runner tag removes him from meaningful scenario consideration.

races.paceDynamic: Hang In There is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Harry Cobden can dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 3m trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. The field is unusually loaded with prominent-running types — Time To Bite, Grand Clermont, Regarde, Imperial Alex and Stratagem are all genuine pace-seeking horses who cannot all secure their natural position, meaning several will be shuffled back and forced to race out of role. With one horse controlling a steady tempo unchallenged, this race is set up to reward those who can travel handily in behind the leader and produce a clean jumping round — the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile is the primary beneficiary, as horses who settle within striking range of Hang In There will avoid the energy cost of racing wide or fighting for position. True hold-up horses will need the pace to quicken significantly to bridge the gap, which a controlled solo-led race on Good ground is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.body: If Hang In There's pace is slightly too slow and a prominent horse tracking it produces a decisive burst from the final fence.

scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace and jumping errors compound to leave the field in a heap and genuine hold-up horses sprint through late.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace and jumping errors compound to leave the field in a heap and genuine hold-up horses sprint through late.

watchPoints.text: Hang In There (Cobden) — watch for any early challenge to its lead from the displaced prominent group; if it is forced to quicken to assert before the halfway mark its stamina over 3m at 168lbs could be compromised fatally.

Time To Bite and Grand Clermont — both natural front-runners who cannot get their position in this shape; if either becomes unruly or wastes energy in the first mile fighting for ground, they become drift risks at short prices and could hamper horses around them.

Riskintheground — Harry Skelton's horse arrives just 21 days after its last run; fitness is assumed but watch the market for any drifting that might suggest the yard has concerns after the quick turnaround.

Ki Woo — at six years old taking on a 3m chase for the first time in competition, watch whether Jack Tudor rides conservatively in the early stages or asks questions of the horse's stamina sooner than ideal.

Hold Your Fort — Callum Pritchard is a conditional who doesn't ride this type of track/class combination regularly; watch whether the hold-up position is executed cleanly or whether the horse gets further back than the race shape requires.

races.name: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Blizzard Of Oz
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who will control the tempo throughout; Won over 23f on Good and holds place in the race shape, but has five poor recent efforts including a fall and a pull-up, and Mullins' 3/20 T14 strike rate suggests the yard is not in peak form — the style advantage is real but current form limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Bold Endeavour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent type who hasn't won on Good going in five attempts at the surface and hasn't scored since a soft-ground run; Henderson T14 at 2/13, but three recent non-completions and a 50-day break make this a tricky profile to trust over this demanding trip.

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural style fits perfectly into this pace scenario; won last time out over 20f on Good and has strong course-compatible form — Cobden takes the ride, Jonjo & A J O'Neill T14 1/14, and a headgear note (p) suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up after inconsistent efforts.

runners_data.name: American Sniper
runners_data.note: Strong stayer with a 2W3P record on similar going and two recent wins over Good ground — David Pipe running at 4/6 T14 strike rate which is excellent; tongue-tie and back-boot noted, held up by Rian Corcoran (5lb claim), and his consistent finishing positions over 19-22f suggest the step up to 23f here is well within range.

runners_data.name: Gabbys Cross
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who should find a position just behind the pace given his natural style isn't displaced; two recent seconds on Good going at distances up to 26f, but the 11-year-old hasn't won for a long time, the yard is 0/10 T14, and the 64-day absence is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Musique De Fee
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with a 3W9P record on Good going across 12 runs at the surface — the most reliable Going record in the field; tongue-tie noted, Mickey Bowen T14 6/34 is a decent recent rate, and three consecutive placings over 26f on Good suggests he handles this sort of trip well.

runners_data.name: Ebony Warrior
runners_data.note: Despite holding a genuinely prominent style — a 3W5P record from 8 Good-ground runs confirms it — he is one of several such horses pushed back in this map because the front positions are full; tongue-tie noted, yard running at 5/8 T14, and his last two wins came over 23f on Good, so the form profile is strong if he can get into a rhythm from a deeper position than ideal.

runners_data.name: Miss Goldfire
runners_data.note: Four wins from 10 on Good ground make her the most strike-rate-prolific horse here by surface, but she naturally wants to race prominent and this map's congestion means she is likely to find herself mid-division against her instincts; tongue-tie worn, Ciaran O'Shea claims 7lb, Harry Fry T14 just 0/2, and she unseated last time — her talent is real but the race shape does not play to her strengths today.

runners_data.name: Escapologist
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent racer who has been nudged back in this map due to the over-supply of horses wanting that position; best form has come at 23-25f on Good (1W3P), tongue-tie and hood noted, Nick Scholfield yard at 0/11 T14, and a third and sixth in recent Good-ground runs suggests he is in consistent if unspectacular form.

runners_data.name: My Gift To You
runners_data.note: Has won four times on Good going from 13 runs and is proven at 26f and 33f, making him one of the better stayers in this field; despite naturally wanting to race prominent, he is displaced rearward in this map — Jonathan Burke rides, James Owen T14 4/47, and his last two runs produced a 1 and 5 which is an encouraging recent pattern.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer (2W8P from 12 runs) who has won over 19-20f and is stepping up significantly in trip here to 23f; displaced from his natural prominent position in this map, Conor Ring rides for a yard 0/3 T14, and while his recent 3-2-1-4-4 form over shorter suggests sound jumping, the trip rise is an untested factor.

races.paceDynamic: Blizzard Of Oz is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over 2m7½f on Good ground at Uttoxeter — a trip that suits a measured pace rather than a sprint. Behind him, Gabbys Cross, Bold Endeavour and Musique De Fee are the most likely to slot into the positions directly behind the leader, as the field contains far more prominent-wanting horses than the front of the race can physically accommodate; Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire, Escapologist, My Gift To You and Oakley are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be squeezed back from their preferred berths and forced to race out of their natural role. With a genuine pace-setter controlling proceedings at a fair but uncontested tempo over this staying trip, the race shape should suit horses that can travel prominently, conserve energy in the early and middle stages, and produce a sustained gallop from the home turn — patient prominent and lightly-restrained midfield trackers are best placed, while the crowded prominent ranks make life harder for those pushed out of position.

scenarios.body: If Blizzard Of Oz dictates an uncontested, fair-tempo gallop and the race develops into a true stamina test from the home turn.

watchPoints.text: Blizzard Of Oz's recent form string (0P1P-5) is deeply concerning — if he fires today he controls everything, but any early sign of jumping hesitancy or lack of fluency could unravel the entire front-running blueprint and hand the tactical advantage to whichever horse travels best behind him.

The cluster of five displaced prominent horses — Ebony Warrior, Miss Goldfire, Escapologist, My Gift To You and Oakley — means the opening circuit at Uttoxeter is at genuine risk of crowding and interference; watch for trouble in running at the first few hurdles as horses fight for positions they naturally want but cannot all have.

Musique De Fee's Going record (12/15 runs on Good) is the strongest surface-match in the field — if he travels smoothly in the prominent group and jumps fluently through the back straight, he becomes a serious shape-fitter in Scenario B and should be tracked throughout.

American Sniper and Crebilly are the truest hold-up horses here and both have winning form on Good ground; if the race is run at a genuinely honest pace from the front, monitor their position approaching the home turn — a clean run from three out is the key condition for either to pose a late threat.

David Pipe's yard is firing at 4/6 over the last 14 days — notably the highest in-form trainer represented in this race — and American Sniper's tongue-tie and back-boot suggest an actively prepared runner; any market support in the build-up would be worth noting given that stable context.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins including two on Good ground at 16f is encouraging form for this 4-year-old, and Harry Skelton on a Dan Skelton runner (16/31 T14) is always a flag; the hood (hg:p) adds a small headgear note, and at 12 days since last run he arrives fresh — his Prominent style means he is best placed of anyone to exploit a weakening Morning Mayhem.

runners_data.note: Tongue-tie applied (hg:t) and 44 days off the track are the key flags for this hold-up runner; similar-going form reads 0 wins from 6 attempts on Good/Soft and the claiming rider (Lewis Saunders 5lb) provides a minor weight relief, but this is the most exposed runner in the field at OR 108 and would need significant assistance from fortune to get involved.

races.paceDynamic: Morning Mayhem is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, holding a Prominent tag and a strong recent record at this 2m trip, meaning this four-runner field is almost certain to unfold at a controlled, single-file tempo from the outset. With no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, Morning Mayhem can dictate entirely on her own terms across Uttoxeter's undulating circuit, setting a sustainable gallop that is unlikely to stretch the field early. Hope Rising and Caelan are both genuine hold-up types who will need late gaps to appear, while Edelak — also Prominent — may track Morning Mayhem closely in second, creating a small lead group with the closers held in behind. This shape strongly favours a horse that can either travel smoothly in Morning Mayhem's slipstream and quicken off a steady pace, or a hold-up runner with the class to close on a front-runner who has not been pressured and arrives at the last with plenty left.

watchPoints.text: Watch Morning Mayhem's jumping — as the sole front-runner in a four-horse field on Good ground, any error at a flight will immediately compress the race and hand the hold-up horses a free run at her.

Edelak's headgear (hood, first-time or retained) should be noted at the off — if she travels smoothly just off Morning Mayhem's pace, Harry Skelton has the experience to time a move that the hold-up horses simply cannot match.

Hope Rising's similar-going record (13/15, 3W 7P) is strikingly strong and Gavin Sheehan will be acutely aware that this field of four means clean passage late is likely — monitor her position from the third-last flight.
Caelan is 44 days since last run with a tongue-tie applied; if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness or sluggish jumping early, she will be irretrievably detached in a field this small.

With only four runners, the actual pace scenario could be even more compressed than predicted — if Edelak elects to sit on Morning Mayhem's heels from the first flight, this could become a two-horse tactical race from very early on, leaving Hope Rising and Caelan needing a late sprint for third.

races.paceDynamic: Kom Tu Voudras is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with Harry Cobden aboard and a tongue tie fitted, will set a controlled, measured gallop over this 2m4f trip on good ground at Uttoxeter — a track that suits hold-up horses less than its wider reputation suggests due to the relatively tight bends. Behind him, Ocean Conquest and Sun Joy will press forward into prominent positions, while Dream's Ka, Gardener, and Suttons Hill will settle in the chasing pack. The field carries more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Ballygeary and Hello Cello are genuine come-from-behind types but will be forced into a midfield berth with other closers present, meaning neither will race in their natural role. With a single uncontested pace-setter likely to dictate a steady-to-honest gallop, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Kom Tu Voudras through the race and challenge approaching the last, rather than hold-up horses who need a true test of stamina to deliver their finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Kom Tu Voudras is the structural key to the whole race — watch whether Harry Cobden is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged or whether Sun Joy and Ocean Conquest force him into a faster tempo than intended from the off.

Ballygeary's natural hold-up style will be compromised if he is squeezed into midfield; watch his early position closely, as racing out of role on a track where getting back from mid-pack is difficult significantly reduces his effectiveness.

Dream's Ka steps up markedly in trip to 2m4f for the first time — watch how he travels through the first circuit, as Harry Skelton may need to use him earlier than ideal if the pace is steady, testing his stamina at this new distance.

Suttons Hill's jumping should be watched carefully given 419 days off and a pull-up last time — any hesitation at the hurdles in the early stages would confirm fitness concerns and signal he is not yet race-ready.

Hello Cello has been redistributed from his natural rear position into midfield; watch whether Ciaran O'Shea elects to drop him back regardless and whether he can find clear daylight to mount a run on the home bend.
